utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, will you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This case is IT-95-4-I, the Prosecutor versus Zeljko Meakic, Momcilo Gruban, and Dusan Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The appearances, please. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, I'm Kapila Waidyaratne, with my colleague Ann Sutherland and the case manager, Gina Butler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. TURLAKOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Sonja Turlakov. I'm an attorney-at-law from Belgrade, and I'm the Defence counsel for Mr. Gruban.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't get it. Could you repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TURLAKOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Sonja Turlakov. I'm an attorney-at-law from Belgrade, and I'm the Defence counsel for Mr. Gruban.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is the initial appearance of the accused Momcilo Gruban. And the accused will be asked to enter a plea on the amended indictment, dated the 18th of July, 2001. Ms. Turlakov, may I take it that your client has received a copy of the amended indictment in a language that he understands and that you have had the opportunity to explain it to him?

utterances.speaker: MS. TURLAKOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my client has received the indictment in a language he understands, and he will enter his plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And does your client wish to have the indictment read out in full, or is he prepared to waive that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. TURLAKOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no need for the indictment to be read out to him in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Then let the accused stand. Mr. Gruban, stand. You have heard what your counsel has said. You've had the indictment in a language you understand, and it has been explained to you. Do you wish to enter your plea today? I'm going to read to you the relevant paragraphs of the indictment and to each you will enter a plea and confine your answers to "guilty" or "not guilty." Paragraph 19.3 of the indictment charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of subordinates in the wilful killing of Omarska prisoners, grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, recognised by Articles 2(a) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.4 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of your subordinates in the murder of Omarska Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. prisoners, violations of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute, and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Convention. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.5 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of subordinates in the murder of Omarska prisoners, crimes against humanity, recognised by Articles 5(a) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.6 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, recognised by Articles 2(b) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.7 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, violations of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal, and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.8 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, crimes against humanity, recognised by Articles 5(f) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.9 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of subordinates in the rape of Omarska prisoners, crimes against humanity, recognised by Articles 5(g) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.10 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of subordinates in wilfully causing great suffering to Omarska prisoners, grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.11 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of subordinates in the commission of outrages upon personal dignity, including humiliating and degrading treatment of the Omarska prisoners, violations of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute and Article 3(1)(c) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.12 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of your subordinates in the unlawful confinement of civilians, grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, recognised by Articles 2(g) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.13 charges you with being criminally responsible for the acts of your subordinates in the unlawful imprisonment of the prisoners of Omarska, crimes against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(e) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. There are just two other matters to be raised. Mr. Prosecutor, I have to make an inquiry about the discharge of your duties under 66(A)(i) to make available to the Defence within 30 days of the Initial Appearance copies of the supporting material which accompany the indictment, and I take it that you will see to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I permitted to state now we are taking steps to disclose the supporting material under Rule 66, and we have spoken to the Defence counsel as we got to know that she had been appointed permanently. And also may I be permitted to state that the Prosecution would be moving to amend the indictment and would be taking steps to give the supporting material to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The next matter is the requirement for fixing a date for the Status Conference. We are required under Rule 65 bis to have a Status Conference within 120 days of the initial appearance. I've been discussing this with the senior legal officer. It seems to me that a date in August would be appropriate, and I'm going to fix the 30th of August as the date for the Status Conference. I will also require the parties to meet with the senior legal officer for any proprietary work which has to be done, and the date for that meeting will be fixed by the senior legal officer in consultation with the parties. Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I be permitted to state also that the Prosecution will be taking appropriate steps to file a general protective measures motion in order to protect the witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we'll await that. Is there any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. TURLAKOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There being no other matters, this hearing stands adjourned.
